extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent agents, IP owners, lawyers, Ministry officials, and courts operating under UAE industrial property law
extracted.subtask_short: UAE patent and industrial property law
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory rules and substantive criteria governing patentability, utility certificates, industrial designs, integrated circuit layout designs, undisclosed information, compulsory licensing, registration, rights, remedies, and procedures in the United Arab Emirates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements (Article 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Patent is granted for every new invention resulting from an inventive idea or an inventive improvement that represents an inventive step and is industrially applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions and tests: 'new' means not preceded by prior industrial technology disclosed to the public before filing or claimed priority date; inventor disclosures within 12 months prior to filing do not affect novelty; inventive step exists if not self-evident to the ordinary man of the profession with respect to prior art; industrial applicability means it can be produced or used in any sector.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection independent of related applications (Article 5(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A Patent may be granted independent of every new application, modification, improvement or addition that responds to an innovation for which a Patent was previously granted, if it fulfills the conditions stipulated in this law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows patenting of improvements/new applications provided statutory conditions are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace period for inventor disclosure (Article 5(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure of information by the inventor or by a third party who obtained the information directly or indirectly from the inventor shall not affect obtaining a Patent if this occurred within 12 months prior to the date of filing the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 12‑month domestic grace period for inventor-originated disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step standard (Article 5(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention shall be deemed to contain an inventive step if it is not self-evident in the opinion of the ordinary man of profession, in relation to the prior art associated with the Patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objective 'person skilled in the art' test phrased as 'ordinary man of profession'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability standard (Article 5(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention shall be industrially applicable if it can be produced or used in any of the sectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad applicability test—manufacture or use in any sector suffices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility Certificate eligibility (Article 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Utility Certificate is granted for every new invention that is industrially applicable but which does not result from a sufficient inventive step to be granted a Patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utility Certificates available where inventive step insufficient for patent; conversion between Utility Certificate and Patent application allowed under executive regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑patentable subject matter (Article 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Patent or Utility Certificate shall not be granted for: a) research, plant or animal species, or biological methods for plant or animal production (except microbiology methods and their products as determined by regs); b) methods of diagnosis, treatment and surgery for humans or animals; c) principles, discoveries, scientific theories and mathematical methods; d) schemes, rules, computer programs, business methods, or purely mental activities, or games; e) natural materials even if purified or isolated (except methods of isolating/purifying natural materials); f) inventions whose exploitation breaches public order or morals or harms life, health or environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Security/military related inventions are subject to special procedures in executive regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor attribution and entitlement (Article 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of the inventor shall be mentioned in the Patent application unless the inventor requests otherwise; rights belong to the inventor or legal successor; if essential elements derived from another person's invention, rights belong to original inventor; joint inventors share rights; mere assistance without inventive contribution does not make one an inventor; where multiple persons independently perform the same invention, the person who files first or claims priority is entitled to the Patent provided application satisfies requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First‑to‑file rule (subject to priority), and clear standards for who qualifies as inventor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer to rightful owner when non‑owner files (Article 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a person who has no right to the invention submits an application, the owner of the right may request the Ministry to transfer the application, Patent, or Utility Certificate to him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural remedy to correct filings by non-right holders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee/invention rules (Article 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: If invention accomplished through execution of a contract, right belongs to the employer unless agreement states otherwise; inventor worker's application within two years from leaving service considered as made during service; inventor entitled to additional compensation if invention's economic value exceeds expectations unless contract sets otherwise; inventions made using employer's expertise/tools/documents in absence of contractual inventive obligation belong to inventor after four months from notifying employer if employer does not express desire to acquire; inventor must notify employer immediately in writing; agreements depriving worker of compensation void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed employer‑employee allocation of rights, notification deadlines, and compensation safeguards for employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal application requirements (Article 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application shall be submitted by inventor, registration agent, or person to whom rights devolved and include applicant name, inventor name, agent (if any), declaration justifying applicant's right if not inventor; name of invention, summary, detailed description, one or more claims, and illustrations (if any); abstract for technical info only; description must be sufficient at filing for skilled person to implement; claims must be clear, concise and entirely based on the description; application and attachments in both Arabic and English; applicant must provide requested information within 90 days; amendments permitted if non‑essential; executive regulations determine attachments/dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict sufficiency and formal-language requirements; 90‑day reply timelines; claims must be supported by description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority from earlier foreign application (Article 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing may express desire to consider priority based on earlier applications filed in a State party to an agreement with the State; application must indicate date, registration number and State; priority period is 12 months from first filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard Paris Convention-style 12‑month priority period for patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination timeline and publication (Article 13)
rubrics_metrics.description: After fees paid, the Ministry shall examine the application and may ask applicant to fulfill requirements; failure to fulfill within 90 days of notification causes deemed waiver of the application; if invention fulfills conditions, Ministry publishes the acceptance in the Industrial Property Bulletin per executive regs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 90‑day cure period during examination; publication upon acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Urgent examination (Article 14)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Ministry may examine certain urgent patent or utility certificate applications before others at applicant request, regardless of filing/exam request date, provided this does not prejudice priority applications and subject to rules in executive regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanism for expedited prosecution subject to regs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity/interrelated inventions and objection handling (Article 15)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may relate to a single invention or a group of related inventions that together constitute one general inventive concept; if more than one invention present, appropriate decision is made per executive regulations; post‑grant finding of lack of interrelation is not a ground to drop the Patent or Utility Certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unity requirement with protection against post‑grant cancellation on this basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division/splitting of applications (Article 16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may split an application containing two or more inventions into two or more applications within limits of original description or drawings; split applications are deemed filed at same time as the first application; executive regulations specify conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisionals allowed and retain original filing date under conditions in regs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant procedures and certificate contents (Article 17)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Center shall grant a Patent/Utility Certificate and publish in Industrial Property Bulletin; the Patent/Utility Certificate is handed to right holder if no objection/re‑examination request or grievance within time in regs; certificate shall contain registration number, date of issuance, statement of payment of registration/renewal fees and other data specified by regs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication and post‑grant objection/re‑examination windows apply; certificate must record fee payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of protection and renewal fees (Article 18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent term is 20 years and Utility Certificate 10 years, each commencing from the date of application; owner must pay annual fees for registration during protection period per executive regulations; executive regulations determine procedures for re‑working applications where fees unpaid or delayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard 20‑year patent term from filing and fee‑maintenance regime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive rights conferred (Article 19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner entitled to exploit the invention: for product inventions this includes manufacture, use, offer for sale, sell, import; for process inventions rights extend to products directly obtained by use of the process and to prevent third parties from using/selling/importing such without consent; rights limited to industrial or commercial purposes and do not extend to acts of protection of the product after sale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines scope of exclusionary rights for product and process patents and limits to commercial/industrial activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior bona fide user defense (Article 20)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who in good faith manufactured the product, used the method, or made serious arrangements for manufacture/use in the State before filing of the application or priority date has the right to continue those activities (without expanding them) despite later grant of Patent/Utility Certificate; that right cannot be transferred except to the establishment benefiting from it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves pre‑filing business interests for bona fide users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment formalities and registration (Article 21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent, Utility Certificate or their applications may be assigned in writing, signed by contracting parties at the Ministry or signatures ratified by notary public; assignment entered in Register after payment of fees; Ministry may refuse registration if it would abuse an industrial property right or harm commercial competition pursuant to executive regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignments must be formalized and are subject to Ministry oversight to prevent abuse/anti‑competitive effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts not covered by patent rights (Article 22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent/Utility Certificate rights do not apply to: activities for education and scientific research; use of patented subject matter in means of transport temporarily or accidentally entering the State (limited to needs of those means); combination of two or more medicines for medical treatment by licensed pharmacist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carves out research/experimental and limited transit/therapeutic exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint owners' unilateral acts and licensing (Article 23)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any joint owner may individually assign or exploit his share and exercise rights conferred unless otherwise agreed or harmful to others; no joint owner may grant a license to others to exploit the invention without agreement among them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects co‑owners while allowing exploitation of individual shares; unanimous consent required for licensing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mortgage of patents (Article 24)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Patent or Utility Certificate may be mortgaged pursuant to controls and procedures in force in the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Security interests in patents permitted under applicable law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory license basic conditions (Article 25)
rubrics_metrics.description: After at least three years from grant, if owner has not exploited or exploited insufficiently, an interested party may request a Compulsory License provided: (a) applicant proved efforts within a reasonable period to obtain license from owner at reasonable price/terms (procedures in regs); (b) license not exclusive; (c) license to meet local market needs and applicant provides guarantees to make sufficient use; (d) licensing decision specifies scope/duration and may include obligations/restrictions; (e) owner granted fair compensation; (f) exploitation limited to licensee and not transferable except upon transfer of licensee's facility with court approval; (g) Articles 29 and 35 apply; (h) for semiconductor technology, compulsory licensing only for general non‑commercial purposes or judicial/administrative corrective practices determined after proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets detailed preconditions and limits for compulsory licensing including three‑year waiting period, requirement to seek voluntary license, and special semiconductor rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal of compulsory license where owner justifies position (Article 25(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A Compulsory License shall not be granted if the owner of the Patent or Utility Certificate justifies his position on legitimate grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court/authority will respect legitimate owner justifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights of compulsory licensee (Article 26)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compulsory License entitles the licensee to carry out some or all acts referred to in Article 19 pursuant to license conditions; licensee may use civil and penal rights granted to owner to protect and exploit if owner fails to do so despite notification or awareness of illegal act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensee gains enforcement powers where owner fails to act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple compulsory licenses allowed (Article 27)
rubrics_metrics.description: Granting a Compulsory License does not preclude grant of other Compulsory Licenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non‑exclusive structure—multiple licensees possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency and public interest exemption (Article 28)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court may not consider requirements in Article 25 if the Compulsory License application is due to an emergency, crisis, disaster, urgent public need, or for non‑commercial purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expedited/relaxed criteria for compulsory licenses in public emergencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory license procedures by court (Article 29)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application for Compulsory License submitted to Court as lawsuit naming applicant and owner; Center notified to attend; Court may give parties time to agree (may extend); if time lapses, Court may grant or refuse license specifying terms/scope and determining compensation; final judgments to be notified and published; judgment effective against third parties only from publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judicial route for compulsory licensing with mediation‑style period and publication rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ministerial compulsory license for public interest (Article 30)
rubrics_metrics.description: By decision of the Minister or authorized person, a Compulsory License may be issued to exploit an invention of importance to public interest under the conditions of Article 25 except the term condition and paragraph (a); decision published in Industrial Property Bulletin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive (ministerial) power to issue compulsory licenses for public interest without waiting periods/voluntary negotiation requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relief where exploitation blocked by earlier patent (Article 31)
rubrics_metrics.description: If it is not possible to exploit an invention in the State without prejudice to rights derived from a previously granted Patent, owner of subsequent Patent may be granted a Compulsory License to the extent necessary if the subsequent invention serves industrial purposes different from the earlier invention or constitutes noticeable technical progress; reciprocal rights for owner of previous Patent; transfer restrictions described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanism to address blocking patents when later innovation depends on earlier patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment and cancellation of compulsory license (Article 32)
rubrics_metrics.description: Court or Minister may amend license conditions at request of owner or licensee if justified by new facts (e.g., contractual license granted with better conditions); may cancel license if licensee breaches conditions or reasons for granting cease to exist; licensee given reasonable period to stop exploiting if immediate cessation causes serious harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ongoing reviewability of compulsory license terms and exit/transition protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and publication of compulsory licenses (Article 33)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compulsory Licenses shall be entered in the Register and published in the Industrial Property Bulletin after fee payment; licenses issued under Article 30 exempted from fees if government agencies exploit the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public record and fee rules for compulsory licenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relinquishment procedures (Article 34)
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner or licensee may relinquish Patent/Utility Certificate by written notification to Ministry and declaring intention publicly; relinquishment may be limited to some rights; cannot prejudice third parties unless they have relinquished in writing; effective against third parties only from publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal relinquishment with publication and third‑party protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidation ground and procedure (Article 35)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any interested party may request the Court to invalidate a Patent, Utility Certificate, or Compulsory License if it was granted without fulfilling the conditions in the law or executive regulations; owner, Ministry and anyone with rights shall be notified; judgment published; invalidation may be limited to part of the Patent/Certificate/License.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judicial review for defects in grant with publication consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of nullity judgment (Article 36)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nullity judgment shall go back to date of granting; however person in whose favor it was issued shall not be obligated to refund compensation obtained from exploiting the invention or the Compulsory License; nullity marked in Register and published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retroactive invalidation with limited restitution obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: International (PCT) applications and fees (Articles 37–38)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ministry shall receive international applications under the PCT; executive regulations govern conditions/procedures; international phase fees/procedures subject to PCT regulations; national phase fees/procedures subject to Articles 11 and 18.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCT national phase governed by UAE filing/examination/fee rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design protection requires registration (Article 40)
rubrics_metrics.description: An industrial design does not enjoy protection under this law unless it is registered in the Register; executive regulations specify submission and examination procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration requirement and procedural rules via executive regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple designs in one application and classification (Article 41)
rubrics_metrics.description: Protection application may include more than one industrial design provided they belong to the same class of the international classification as determined by executive regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows multiple designs per filing subject to classification constraint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design priority and term (Articles 42, 45)
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority provisions analogous to Article 12 apply with six months priority term for industrial designs; protection term of industrial design is 20 years from filing; annual fees due during protection period; executive regs define re‑working for unpaid/delayed fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Six‑month design priority and 20‑year term with maintenance fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design novelty and public order limits (Article 43)
rubrics_metrics.description: Industrial design shall be novel; may not be commercially exploited if violating public order or morals; deemed novel unless disclosed to public by publication, use or other method prior to filing; disclosures within one year prior to filing are not deemed public disclosure for purposes of novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One‑year grace period for design disclosures and public‑order limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design examination procedure and 90‑day cure (Article 44)
rubrics_metrics.description: Center shall examine industrial design application after fee payment and may request fulfillment of requirements within 90 days; failure deemed relinquishment; designs meeting conditions published in Industrial Property Bulletin; requirements/procedures determined by exec regs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parallel 90‑day response period as for patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality standard for integrated circuit layout designs (Article 55)
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrated Circuit Layout Designs enjoy protection if original, outcome of intellectual effort by owner, and not among general knowledge common to practitioners in the relevant industrial art; original if coupling/connection of components is original even if components are within general knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects layout designs based on originality of arrangement/connection rather than individual components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjects not protected within layout designs (Article 56)
rubrics_metrics.description: No concept, method, technical system, or coded information included in an Integrated Circuit Layout Design shall enjoy protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excludes functional/technical elements and code from layout design protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited uses without permission for layout designs (Article 57)
rubrics_metrics.description: Without prior written permission from owner, reproduction of all or part of original layout design (including incorporation into an integrated circuit) and importing/selling/distributing a layout design for business purposes is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad exclusive rights over reproduction and commercial distribution of layout designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted acts without license for layout designs (Article 58)
rubrics_metrics.description: Permitted without license: reproduction/commercial exploitation by a person who did not know the layout was protected (subject to fair compensation to dispose of stock); personal use/testing/analysis/teaching/training/scientific research (creator of new layout may protect it); independent creation identical by independent efforts; importing protected layout design or integrated circuit produced using protected layout design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defenses include innocent infringement, research/teaching, independent creation and import allowances; remedial fair‑compensation requirement for innocent possessors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layout design registration and term (Article 59)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for registration submitted to Center per executive regs; term of protection 10 years from date of application or first commercial exploitation in State or abroad, whichever earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ten‑year term measured from filing or first exploitation (earlier).

rubrics_metrics.name: Undisclosed information protection conditions (Article 61)
rubrics_metrics.description: Undisclosed information enjoys protection provided: (1) confidentiality so that components/composition not known or circulated in general to those engaged in the industrial art; (2) derives commercial value from being secret; (3) depends on effective measures taken by legal holder to preserve it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopts trade‑secret style requirements—secrecy, commercial value, and reasonable protective measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of protection for undisclosed information and gov't submissions (Article 62)
rubrics_metrics.description: Protection extends to undisclosed information resulting from great efforts submitted to government agencies to allow marketing of pharmaceutical/agrichemical products; government agencies receiving such are obligated to protect it until confidentiality ceases or for a period not exceeding five years, whichever less; disclosure by authorities allowed for protecting the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited protection period for regulatory submissions and public-interest disclosure carve‑outs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties and liability of legal holder of undisclosed information (Article 63)
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal holder obligated to take necessary measures to preserve information, limit circulation within facility to specialists, and prevent leakage; holder liable for infringement by third parties unless he proves sufficient and reasonable efforts to preserve it; confidentiality and rights remain while information undisclosed per Article 61.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Burden on holder to implement and prove reasonable protective practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts contrary to honest business practices and unfair competition (Article 64)
rubrics_metrics.description: Acts considered inconsistent with honest business practices include bribery of employees to obtain information; inciting employees to disclose information learned by virtue of jobs; disclosure by contractors under confidentiality contracts; obtaining information by theft/espionage/illegal methods; obtaining information by fraudulent methods; use by third party of information obtained by such acts knowing it is confidential; any other inconsistent acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates unlawful means of acquiring undisclosed information and equates them with unfair competition/infringement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted means of obtaining information (Article 65)
rubrics_metrics.description: Not inconsistent with honest commercial practices: obtaining information from public sources; obtaining via independent efforts including examination/testing/analysis of commodities that include undisclosed information; obtaining via scientific research/innovation by independent diligent persons; possession/use of known/available information circulated among those engaged in the relevant art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits legitimate reverse engineering, independent creation and public‑source acquisition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies: damages and provisional measures (Articles 67–68)
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner or licensee may request Court to award compensation for damage from infringement; may request precautionary seizure order for inventions, designs, layout designs, facilities or parts thereof exploiting industrial property in event of infringement or illegal acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Civil remedies include damages and provisional seizure powers to prevent ongoing infringement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal and civil penalties for false documents, imitation and willful infringement (Article 69)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party submitting false documents or incorrect information to obtain a Patent/Utility Certificate/design/layout, or anyone who imitates an invention or willfully infringes any right, shall be sentenced to imprisonment and fined not less than 100,000 dirhams and not more than 1,000,000 dirhams, or either penalty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant criminal sanctions for fraud and willful infringement; imprisonment possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confiscation, destruction and publication orders (Article 70)
rubrics_metrics.description: Court may rule to confiscate impounded object, order destruction or removal of effects of illegal activities and machines/tools used for infringement; Court may order that the judgment be published in Industrial Property Bulletin or local daily newspapers at convict's expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remedies include destruction and public shaming via publication of judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial police designation for Ministry employees (Article 71)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ministry employees designated by decision of Minister of Justice in agreement with the Minister shall have capacity of judicial police officers in proving violations within their jurisdiction of this law, its executive regulations and implementation decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empowers designated Ministry personnel to act in investigative/enforcement roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance and opposition procedures and committee (Article 74)
rubrics_metrics.description: A grievance Committee shall be formed by Cabinet decision headed by a judge and two IP experts (not Center employees); committee procedures, duration and remuneration specified; Minister appoints Secretary; committee decides grievances against decisions in application of law and regs subject to prescribed fee; committee does not consider registration grievances except after opposition with the Center via request for re‑examination after granting; exec regs determine re‑examination controls/terms; lawsuits generally not accepted by Courts except after grievance filed before Committee (subject to clause 5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative grievance pathway required prior to court in many registration disputes; committee makeup and fee rules prescribed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration agents profession conditions (Article 75)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration agents may practice only after being registered in the Ministry's agents’ registration list and paying prescribed fee; executive regulations specify conditions, duties, practice provisions and administrative penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensing/registration requirement for professional representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees, executive regulations, repeal and enforcement timing (Articles 76–80)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cabinet of Ministers issues fees necessary to implement the law upon proposal of Minister of Finance; executive regulations to be issued within six months of publication; Federal Law No. 17 of 2002 repealed; prior regulations/decisions continue to apply insofar as not conflicting until necessary new regulations issued; law published in Official Gazette and comes into force six months after publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative and transitional provisions governing implementation timetable, fee-setting, repeal and continuity.
